text: When an ECP5 conv2d reduction is timing-limited at 53 MHz by an 18.8 ns window-FF -> MULT18X18D -> 25-input depth-5 adder-tree path with tree_regs=0 and no multiplier output register, add a fabric register after each multiplier and one per tree level (tree_regs 0->3, pipe_mul 0->1) to split the reduction, reaching 119 MHz (+65.4 MHz) while dropping 56 LUTs and keeping 9 DSPs.

When an ECP5 conv2d is feasible at 118.6 MHz with the critical path on the line-buffer BRAM output (lb_mem 5.83 ns) rather than the adder tree, narrow acc_width from 24 to the legal minimum of 22, which cut 14 LUTs and raised Fmax to 121.3 MHz (+2.7 MHz) with DSP=9 and 1.0 px/cycle unchanged because the adder tree was not timing-critical.

When an ECP5 conv2d is already feasible at 121.3 MHz and your objective is LUT minimization, increase multiplier/tree pipelining from 1 to 2 stages to cut 4 LUTs with no DSP change, but expect Fmax to slip to 119.8 MHz because the 5.83 ns line-buffer BRAM read (lb_mem1.0.0) feeding the window shift register still dominates the critical path.

When an ECP5 conv2d’s critical path is the DP16KD line-buffer clock-to-out (5.83 ns logic) feeding the window FF and the design is already feasible at 119.8 MHz, do not raise pipe_mul from 2 to 3: it leaves LUT/DSP at 632/9 and costs 7.2 MHz (to 112.6 MHz) by increasing routing on that unchanged path (LUT route 0.69→0.88 ns, FF route 1.60→1.93 ns), so pipeline the BRAM-to-FF interface instead.

When an ECP5 conv2d is already feasible and BRAM-bound (lb_mem1.0.0 read 5.83 ns dominates the 8.88 ns path, 112.6 MHz, 632 LUT, 9 DSP), don't push multiplier output registers into the hard DSP output regs expecting fabric savings, since it leaves fmax/LUT/DSP unchanged (112.5872573852539 MHz, 632 LUT, 9 DSP) and only the BRAM read, not the multiplier/adder, sets the clock.

On ECP5 conv2d, when the BRAM read path lb_mem1.0.0 (5.83 ns) plus win LUT/route caps fmax near 113 MHz while the design is already feasible and throughput-saturated, push the multiplier output and in/out registers into the hard DSP block to offload fabric LUT/FF from the multiply path, raising fmax 112.6 to 125.7 MHz (+13.1 MHz) with 2 fewer LUTs and no DSP-count change (9).

On ECP5 conv2d, with the critical path already on the 5.83 ns BRAM read plus a window LUT into a TRELLIS_FF and only LUT left to trim, do not push both multiplier input and output registers into the DSP block (in_out), because it leaves LUT=630 and DSP=9 unchanged and drops Fmax from 125.7 to 115.4 MHz by rerouting the non-DSP path.

On ECP5 conv2d designs already timing-feasible but LUT-bound, when the 8.18 ns critical path is a routing-dominated 24-bit adder/reduction tree of LUT4s into a carry chain rather than BRAM or multipliers, narrow the accumulator to 21 bits and add 2 tree pipeline stages plus a post-multiplier register to cut LUTs from 289 to 255 and raise Fmax from 122.3 to 140.5 MHz by letting yosys restructure the reduction into fewer/wider LUT4s.

On ECP5 conv2d, when a feasible 127.6 MHz design has a routing-dominated 7.84 ns path through a 24-bit, 9-cell carry-chain adder tree, narrowing the accumulator to its 21-bit minimum and inserting one tree register cuts 17 LUTs and lifts Fmax to 135.9 MHz by shortening the carry chain and splitting the long out_data route.

On ECP5 conv2d, when the critical path is only a 5.83 ns DP16KD line-buffer read plus a 1.16 ns-routed window LUT (7.36 ns total) and the multiplier/reduction tree has slack, add a second tree register plus one multiplier pipeline stage (dsp_regs=out changed nothing at 0 DSPs) to retime the LUT fabric, cutting LUTs 272→259 and the window-LUT route 1.16→0.93 ns for +4.4 MHz (135.9→140.3 MHz).

When the ECP5 conv2d critical path is BRAM-bound at 140 MHz by the DP16KD line-buffer read (5.83 ns) plus a LUT/route and throughput/acc_width are at structural limits, add one more tree register and multiplier pipeline stage (tree_regs 2→3, pipe_mul 1→2) to cut LUTs by 45 (259→214) with only +0.4 MHz fmax impact because the added stages are hidden behind the BRAM path.

On ECP5 conv2d, when LUT count is the only remaining objective and the critical path is the DP16KD line-buffer read (5.83 ns) plus window mux/route to FF (7.11 ns total, 140.7 MHz), raise pipe_mul from 2 to 3: it saves 1 LUT (214->213) at only 0.5 MHz fmax cost (140.7->140.2 MHz) because the path stays in the line-buffer/mux and not the multiplier.

When an ECP5 conv2d is already at 1 px/cycle and timing-limited by a routing-dominated 24-bit LUT4/carry-chain reduction into out_data (127.6 MHz, 289 LUTs), narrow the accumulator to the 21-bit legal minimum, add 2 tree pipeline stages, and register the multiplier output so yosys can fold the carry-chain reduction into fewer/wider LUT4s, yielding +13.8 MHz (141.4 MHz) and -34 LUTs.

On ECP5 conv2d, when already feasible near 141 MHz and LUT-critical on a 5.83 ns lb_mem1.0.0 logic path, add the multiplier input pipeline only to reduce LUTs: pipe_mul [1,0] cut 11 LUTs but dropped Fmax to 140.6 MHz because the unchanged lb_mem line-buffer logic, not the multiplier or tree, still dominates the critical path.

When an ECP5 conv2d is already feasible at 140.6 MHz with its LUT-logic critical path dominated by 5.83 ns of lb_mem1.0.0 logic versus only 0.92 ns of win[0] routing, do not add tree_regs [2,1], since it raised LUTs 244→272 and cut Fmax to 135.9 MHz (-4.6 MHz) without shortening the fixed logic delay.

When an ECP5 conv2d is already feasible but LUT-heavy with its critical path set by the DP16KD line-buffer read (5.83 ns) plus window LUT routing, set tree_regs=3 and pipe_mul=1: this folds product/reduction LUTs, cutting LUTs 272->214 and window route 1.16->0.89 ns for +5.3 MHz (135.9->141.2 MHz), though the unchanged 5.83 ns line-buffer read still caps further gain.

On an ECP5 conv2d already feasible at 141.2 MHz with a 7.08 ns critical path through lb_mem1 DP16KD read (5.83 ns) plus win[0] LUT/route, do not retune tree_regs 3->2, pipe_mul 1->0, or dsp_regs out->in_out: it costs +45 LUTs (214->259) and -0.9 MHz (141.2->140.3) at unchanged DSP count, because the multiplier/tree fabric has slack and the path stays line-buffer-bound.

On ECP5 conv2d, when already feasible and LUT-bound with the critical path dominated by the DP16KD line-buffer read (5.83 ns), raise tree_regs to 3 to split the carry-chain reduction, cutting LUTs 259->208 with Fmax held at ~140.5 MHz (140.31->140.55) because the added reduction registers are off the line-buffer-dominated path.

When an ECP5 conv2d reduction tree is routing-limited at 127.6 MHz by a 24-bit adder carry chain (3.4 ns LUT4 route into 9 cells) with tree_regs=0 and 0 DSP, narrow the accumulator to its legal 21-bit minimum and add 3 tree registers with 2 multiplier pipeline stages so synthesis merges reduction LUT4s instead of routing them, gaining +13.6 MHz (141.2 MHz) and -75 LUTs at 0 DSP.

On ECP5 conv2d, when the critical path is a 7.08 ns lb_mem1.0.0 LUT-logic path (5.83 ns logic, no routing) rather than the multiplier/accumulator tree, do not add tree_regs [3,2] and pipe_mul [2,1], since it costs 41 LUTs (214→255) for only +0.18 MHz (141.20→141.38) because retiming the multiplier/tree cannot shorten the bottleneck register path.

On ECP5 conv2d at 1 px/cycle (3x3/8-bit/width-640, 9 multipliers, 255 LUTs, 141.4 MHz), do not insert tree_regs=[2,1]: it added 25 LUTs and lost 0.8 MHz (140.5 MHz) because the 5.83 ns lb_mem1.0.0 LUT logic stayed critical, so only pipe the reduction tree after restructuring that logic.

When an ECP5 conv2d is BRAM-bound (DP16KD line-buffer clock-to-out = 5.83 of 7.11 ns) and LUT-heavy at 280, retime deeper with tree_regs 1->3 and pipe_mul 1->3 to cut 66 LUTs (280->214) for only +0.12 MHz Fmax (140.55->140.67 MHz), because the critical path remains the BRAM read rather than the multiplier/adder tree.

When an ECP5 3x3/8-bit conv2d is BRAM-bound at ~141 MHz by the DP16KD line-buffer clock-to-out of 5.83 ns plus the win[0] LUT route, do not shift retiming from tree_regs=3 to 2 or deepen multiplier retiming to cut LUT—it added +45 LUT and -0.4 MHz with no feasibility change because the critical path never enters the multiplier/adder cloud.

When an ECP5 conv2d reduction is LUT-bound with a routing-dominated 24-bit carry-chain path (3.4 ns route in out_data LUT4, tree_regs=0, pipe_mul=0), narrow the accumulator to its legal 21-bit minimum and add 3 tree and 2 multiplier pipeline registers so yosys merges LUT4s into wider cells (-75 LUT to 214, +13.6 MHz to 141.2 MHz) while holding throughput.

When the ECP5 conv2d critical path is already routing-dominated (5.83 ns logic in the win[0] LUT/ROM chain, 7.08 ns total), cutting pipeline registers (tree_regs 3->1, pipe_mul 2->0) to save LUTs instead adds 58 LUTs (214->272) and drops Fmax from 141.2 to 135.9 MHz, because de-registering simply lengthens the fabric route (0.89->1.16 ns on win[0]) rather than removing logic.

When an ECP5 conv2d is already at 1.0 px/cycle and LUT-bound by a routing-dominated reduction (lb_mem1.0.0, 7.36 ns), insert 2 tree pipeline stages and 1 multiplier pipeline stage: LUTs drop 17 (272→255) and Fmax rises 5.4 MHz (135.9→141.4) because the extra registers shorten the LUT4/route path (1.16→0.88 ns) without using DSPs.
